land.text: the Kathmandu Valley, with settlement east toward Banepa, west toward Tistung Deurali and northwest toward Gorkha

successors.note: The Thakuri page: Raghava Deva "is said to have founded a ruling dynasty in 879 CE" and Thakuri rule began "When the Lichchavi rule ended". The Licchavi page's own text gives c. 450-c. 750, while its list runs on to Mandeva IV (875-879).

capitals.name: Kathmandu Valley (Licchavi court; Kailashkut Bhawan at Hadigaun under Amshuvarman)
capitals.note: No page opened names a capital: the Licchavi page mentions Kathmandu only as where the clan settled and the Amshuverma page describes Kailashkut Bhawan as a palace "believed to have been located about Hadigaun in Kathmandu". Coordinates are the valley (researcher's).

rulers.name: Mānadeva I
rulers.note: the page: "approximate only, especially with respect to dates"; earliest inscription 464

rulers.name: Aṃshuvarmā
rulers.note: a prime minister who "assumed the throne"; mahasamanta from about 598 (Amshuverma page)

rulers.name: Narendradeva
rulers.note: restored "with the Tibetan Empire's help" in around 643 (Narendradeva page)

correction.text: the Kathmandu Valley, with settlement east toward Banepa, west toward Tistung Deurali and northwest toward Gorkha

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Licchavi row; its Kathmandu row begins 1202 at 661 km2). The page says the kingdom was "in the Kathmandu Valley" and that settlement "extended east toward Banepa, west toward Tistung Deurali, and northwest toward present-day Gorkha"; it gives no area and no frontier, and is silent on any Gandak, Kosi or Tibetan border. The Tibetan Empire's Cliopatria shape does not touch the valley (checked 640-800).

region.text: the Kathmandu Valley, with settlement east toward Banepa, west toward Tistung Deurali and northwest toward Gorkha

ledger.note: 464: the earliest dated record of the Licchavi kingdom of Nepal. "The earliest known physical record of the kingdom is an inscription of Mānadeva, which dates from 464"; it names three earlier rulers, so the kingdom is older (the page says "approximately 450").

region.text: the Kathmandu Valley, with settlement east toward Banepa, west toward Tistung Deurali and northwest toward Gorkha

ledger.note: 879: Licchavi rule gives way to the Thakuris. Raghava Deva "is said to have founded a ruling dynasty in 879 CE" and Nepal Sambat "began on 20 October, 879 CE"; the Licchavi list ends with Mandeva IV (875-879). The Licchavi page's intro dates the kingdom "approximately 450 to 750 CE".

wars.name: Narendradeva's restoration
wars.outcome: After the ouster of Narendradeva's father "in around 624", the family fled to Tibet; Narendradeva "with the Tibetan Empire's help, reclaimed his ancestral throne from them in around 643" and sent envoys to China (Wang Xuance, c. 648).
wars.note: The Amshuverma page says only that Udayadeva "was exiled to Tibet", with no year. Neither page calls Nepal a Tibetan dependency; the Tibetan dossier should decide any vassal tint.

certainty.note: No frontier is given on any page; only the Kathmandu Valley is certain.

notes: Cliopatria has no Licchavi row (the brief names Nepal's Licchavis as a gap). Four thin pages: none gives an area, a frontier, a capital or a Tibetan overlordship. The Licchavi infobox/intro says c. 450-c. 750 but its list continues to Mandeva IV (875-879) and the Thakuri page begins in 879, so the dossier runs to 879 and flags the conflict. The valley radius (35 km) is the researcher's reading of 'Kathmandu Valley' with its listed spread; if gap-fillers find the Gandak-Kosi extent in Chinese sources it should replace it. Thin pages do not date the 7th-century Tibetan-Nepalese relationship as vassalage; no vassal events recorded.
